ex.simple.title: Your devices, connected from any network
ex.simple.desc: An exchange server on the internet in the middle. Home and office Windows PCs share folders, a laptop sends and receives media, one phone opens any folder and another shares its own, and a watch and a TV receive media - all through the server.
ex.simple.sub: One exchange server on the internet. Every device signs in to your account and finds the others.
ex.simple.foot: No port forwarding: every device dials out to the server, from any network.
ex.scheme.title: Access from anywhere through the exchange server
ex.scheme.desc: Detailed scheme. The exchange server at a public address keeps accounts, enrolled devices, the directory of folders and broadcasts, and a user log. Windows PCs with Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows share folders over SFTP and work as clients; Android phones open any of those folders or share their own; a watch and an Android TV receive media. Every device keeps a control connection to the server; folders open through data tunnels the server splices.
ex.scheme.sub: Who connects to whom, and what travels where
ex.how.title: How it works
ex.how.1:
Each device signs in once with your login and keeps
a device token - never the password.
ex.how.2:
A PC or a phone publishes its shared folders
to your account's directory.
ex.how.3:
Any other device lists all your folders
and attaches the ones it needs.
ex.how.4:
Opening a folder asks for a tunnel: the server joins
the two outgoing connections and reads no bytes.
ex.scheme.internet: Internet - any network: home Wi-Fi, office, mobile data, hotel, carrier NAT
ex.dev.homepc.sub:
SFTP server: D:\Photos
and a client on the same PC
ex.dev.laptop.sub:

ex.dev.phone.sub:

ex.dev.phonesrv.sub:
shares its own
folders as SFTP
and opens others
ex.scheme.foot1: A folder you share with someone outside your account travels by its own share link, not by your login.
ex.scheme.foot2: On one Wi-Fi the devices still connect directly; the server is the route that works from everywhere else.
ex.steps.title: How a folder opens through the exchange server
ex.steps.desc: Five steps: sign in, publish a folder, list your folders, connect through a tunnel, open the folder over end-to-end encrypted SFTP.
ex.steps.sub: From a PC at home to a phone anywhere - five steps, no router settings
ex.steps.1.b:
Each device joins
your account once
with a login or
a pairing code
ex.steps.2.b:
The PC announces
its shared folders
to your directory
ex.steps.3.b:
The phone sees
all your folders
on all your devices
ex.steps.4.b:
The server asks
the PC to dial back
and joins the two lines
ex.steps.5.b:
SFTP runs
end to end, inside
the encrypted tunnel
ex.steps.foot: The server only splices the two connections - inside it sees encrypted SSH, never your files.
ex.keeps.title: What the exchange server keeps
ex.keeps.desc: Three columns. On its disk: accounts with password hashes, enrolled devices, folder names, a user log. In memory only: folder access codes while a device is online, live tunnels and relay buffers, pairing codes. Never: your files, secrets in the log, your list for anyone outside your account.
ex.keeps.sub: Built so that running a server never means handing it your media

only while the device

Live tunnels and the last

One-time pairing codes,

ex.keeps.never.2:
Passwords, tokens or

Your list - to anyone

br.simple.title: Live broadcast: any device on air, every device listening
br.simple.desc: A phone camera, a watch microphone and a Windows PC screen broadcast through the exchange server relay to a phone, a watch, an Android TV and a Windows PC.
br.simple.sub: Camera, microphone or screen - one upload, any number of your devices watching.
br.simple.lan: On one Wi-Fi the stream goes direct
br.simple.foot: Ask a chosen device to start playing with Cast - it asks before it plays.
br.scheme.title: Live broadcast across devices and networks
br.scheme.desc: Detailed scheme. Broadcasters: an Android phone with camera and microphone, a Wear OS watch microphone with up to four listeners, a Windows PC screen, camera and system sound. The exchange server lists live broadcasts, relays one upload to any number of listeners keeping only the last two seconds, routes Cast requests and offers tunnels. Receivers: an Android phone, a watch, an Android TV and a Windows PC. On one Wi-Fi the stream goes direct.
br.scheme.sub: Who goes on air, how the stream travels, who plays it
br.b.phone.sub:
camera + microphone
video with sound, video only or audio only
H.264 and AAC in MPEG-TS
br.b.watch.sub:
microphone, AAC audio
up to 4 listeners at once
br.b.pc.sub:
screen, camera, microphone, system sound
Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows
br.r.pc.sub: Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows, StreamsPlayer
br.scheme.lan: Same Wi-Fi: direct to the broadcaster, lowest delay
br.srv.directory: Directory: which broadcasts are live now
br.srv.relay: Fan-out relay: one upload, many listeners
br.srv.buffer:
Keeps only the last 2 s: a slow listener
skips ahead, never falls behind
br.srv.cast: Cast: asks a chosen device to start playing
br.srv.tunnel: Tunnel for players that need RTSP or HTTP
br.srv.log: Log: who started what, without stream ids
br.scheme.order: Route order for every receiver: same Wi-Fi first, then the relay, then a tunnel.
br.order.title: Which way the stream travels
br.order.desc: Three routes in the order a receiver tries them: direct on the same network, the exchange server relay, a tunnel through the server.
br.order.sub: The receiver tries the routes in this order and starts from the top after any reconnect.
br.order.1.b:
Phone, watch and PC on one Wi-Fi: the receiver connects straight
to the broadcaster. Nothing leaves the house.
br.order.2.b:
The broadcaster uploads once; the server hands the stream
to every listener. Works from any network.
br.order.3.b:
One line per listener, for players that need the original
RTSP or HTTP address.
br.cast.title: Cast: start playback on another device
br.cast.desc: An office Windows PC broadcasts its screen through the exchange server and casts it to the living-room TV, which asks, accepts and plays the stream from the relay.
br.cast.sub: Example: the office PC shares its screen, the living-room TV plays it
br.cast.1: The PC goes on air and uploads once
br.cast.2: On the PC: Cast to Living-room TV
br.cast.3: The TV asks: play the broadcast from Office PC?
br.cast.4: Accepted - the answer returns to the PC
br.cast.5: The TV plays the stream from the relay
home.simple.title: Home network: your storage, reachable from outside
home.simple.desc: A home network with a router, a media PC running an SFTP server, a phone and a TV on Wi-Fi. Outside, a phone on mobile data and a laptop in a hotel reach the PC through the router's public address.
home.simple.sub: No exchange server: a fixed address, an SFTP server and one rule on the router.
home.simple.away1.sub:
reaches home through
the public address
home.simple.away2.sub:
the same folder,
from any city
home.simple.router.sub:
forwards one port
to the PC
home.simple.pc.sub:
SFTP server
with a fixed address
home.simple.foot: At home the app uses the local address, away the public one - it picks by itself.
home.scheme.title: Home network without an exchange server
home.scheme.desc: Detailed scheme. Outside devices connect to the router's public address 203.0.113.25 or a dynamic DNS name. The router forwards TCP 2222 to the media PC at 192.168.1.20 and TCP 2223 to the phone server at 192.168.1.42, both with reserved addresses. Devices inside the home network connect to the servers directly.
home.scheme.sub: Fixed local addresses, port forwarding and a public address - nothing else in between
home.public.title: Public address
home.public.sub:
a static IP 203.0.113.25
or a dynamic DNS name
myhome.example.net
home.scheme.pc.sub:
Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows
SFTP 192.168.1.20:2222
fixed address, folders D:\Media
home.scheme.lan2.sub:
plays from the PC
over the LAN
home.note.order: Each resource stores both addresses: the local one first, the public one when away.
home.note.cgnat: No public IP from your provider (carrier NAT)? Use the exchange server instead.
home.steps.title: Your home storage, reachable from outside, in six steps
home.steps.desc: Six steps: fix the storage address, turn on the SFTP server, forward a port, get a public address, pair devices by QR code, use the same folder at home and away.
home.steps.sub: One SFTP server, the router you already have, no exchange server
home.steps.1.b:
Reserve 192.168.1.20 for the PC in the
router's DHCP settings - it never changes.
home.steps.2.b:
Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows shares folders;
a phone shares its own from Settings.
home.steps.3.b:
On the router: TCP 2222 from the internet
to 192.168.1.20:2222. One port per server.
home.steps.4.b:
A static IP from your provider, or a free
dynamic DNS name that follows a changing one.
home.steps.5.b:
Scan the server's code: the folder arrives
with all its addresses and its trusted key.
home.steps.6.b:
At home it connects locally, away through
the public address - the same folder.
home.pair.title: One code, three addresses
home.pair.desc: A Windows PC running Share Manager shares D:\Media over SFTP at 192.168.1.20:2222 and produces a QR code or an .fmscfg file. The phone that scanned it receives three addresses and tries them at once: the home Wi-Fi address 192.168.1.20:2222, the IPv6 address 2001:db8:25::20 and the internet address myhome.example.net:2222 through the router's forwarded port. It uses the fastest one that answers.
home.pair.sub: Share Manager writes every way to reach your PC into one QR code or .fmscfg file
home.pair.phone.s:
scanned the code
or opened the file
home.pair.lanes: All three are tried at once - preferred in the order 1, 2, 3
home.pair.1.b:
Fastest: a direct connection
over the home network
home.pair.2.b:
Works even behind carrier NAT, when your
provider gives the PC an IPv6 address
home.pair.3.b:
Through the router's forwarded port,
from anywhere
home.pair.foot: The phone picks the fastest address that answers; the PC's host key is pinned at the first pairing.
home.pair.foot2: A phone on the same Wi-Fi also finds the PC by itself if its address changed.

hero.title: One family of apps, every device
hero.desc: Phones, a watch, a TV, a VR headset, a laptop, a Windows PC, a router and a phone acting as a server, all connected around the exchange server.
hero.sub: FastMediaSorter on phones, TV, watch and VR - Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows on PCs
sc.folders-exchange.title: A folder of another device, through your exchange server
sc.folders-exchange.desc: Six steps: add your exchange server on both devices, share a folder on the first, switch on Access from anywhere, find the folder under From my devices on the second, attach it, and open it from any network.
sc.folders-exchange.sub: One entry per folder - the app tries the local address first, then the server
sc.folders-exchange.1.b:
On both devices:
Settings, General, My devices,
Add server
sc.folders-exchange.2.b:
On the first device: Share over SFTP,
add the folder, switch the server on
sc.folders-exchange.3.b:
In the same card, switch it on
and choose the outgoing server
sc.folders-exchange.4.b:
On the second device: Add Resource,
From my devices
sc.folders-exchange.5.b:
One entry per folder - the same one
at home and away
sc.folders-exchange.6.b:
Local address first, then through
the server. Read-only is your choice
sc.folders-drive.title: Files between your devices via Google Drive
sc.folders-drive.desc: Four steps: sign in to the same Google account on both devices, switch on Files via Google Drive on both, send files or open a folder of the other device, and wait for its answer.
sc.folders-drive.sub: No exchange server and no address - your own Google account is the box
sc.folders-drive.1.b:
Sign in to Google on both devices.
The channel never leaves your account
sc.folders-drive.2.b:
Settings, Pending device transfers:
Files via Google Drive, on both
sc.folders-drive.3.b:
Send to.. a device, or open its folder
from My devices - via Google Drive
sc.folders-drive.4.b:
The other device answers when it checks:
about a minute with its app open, every
15 minutes in the background if allowed
sc.broadcast-start.title: Going on air from your phone
sc.broadcast-start.desc: Four steps: open Live Broadcast, choose what goes out - sound, camera, the screen or a file - start, then give the link or the QR code to the listeners.
sc.broadcast-start.sub: The password goes separately: the link and the QR code never carry it
sc.broadcast-start.1.b:
Live Broadcast: Audio only, Camera +
audio, Camera only, Broadcast the
screen or Broadcast a file
sc.broadcast-start.2.b:
Screen: the system asks for consent
every session; the picture has no sound
sc.broadcast-start.3.b:
Show the QR code, send the link or the
descriptor file. Tell the password
another way: they never carry it
sc.broadcast-start.4.b:
Devices of your account see it in
Broadcasts of my devices, if the phone
is signed in to an exchange server
sc.broadcast-receive.title: Four ways to open a broadcast
sc.broadcast-receive.desc: Four ways to a broadcast: the list Broadcasts of my devices, a link or a QR code or a file, a link with a password, or a cast that another of your devices sends to this one.
sc.broadcast-receive.sub: Nothing is found on the local network by itself - you open it, or it is cast to you
sc.broadcast-receive.1.b:
Streams, Broadcasts of my devices:
what the devices of your account
broadcast right now
sc.broadcast-receive.2.t: A link, a QR code or a file
sc.broadcast-receive.2.b:
Open the link, scan the QR code or
choose the descriptor file
sc.broadcast-receive.3.b:
Enter the password you were given
separately - the link does not carry it
sc.broadcast-receive.4.b:
Another of your devices casts it here.
This device asks before it plays
sc.watch.title: The watch on your account, with or without the phone
sc.watch.desc: Six steps: the exchange server is added on the phone, Connect watch in its card menu, the phone asks the server for a pairing code and hands it to the watch, the watch joins the account, then works over its own Wi-Fi or LTE, and the phone may stay away.
sc.watch.sub: Bluetooth carries the hand-over and commands; the data goes over the watch's own network
sc.watch.1.b:
My devices: the exchange server is
already added and signed in
sc.watch.2.b:
In the server card menu choose
Connect watch. Keep the watch
nearby and unlocked
sc.watch.3.b:
The phone asks the server for a one-use
pairing code and hands it over. No
password is typed on the watch
sc.watch.4.b:
It gets its own entry in the account.
Bluetooth carried only the hand-over
sc.watch.5.b:
Wi-Fi or LTE: folders of the account,
the broadcast list, casts, Send to..
sc.watch.6.b:
Needed again only after the watch is
signed out or its entry is removed
sc.schedule.title: A schedule over folders of other devices
sc.schedule.desc: Four steps: open Manage scheduled operations and Add, choose a folder of another device as the source or the destination, pick New since last run with copy or move, then check History.
sc.schedule.sub: A side that cannot be reached skips the run - nothing breaks and nothing is lost
sc.schedule.1.b:
Settings, Manage scheduled operations,
then Add
sc.schedule.2.b:
The source or the destination can be a
folder of another device, through its
server or via Google Drive
sc.schedule.3.b:
Copy, move or delete. New since last
run takes only what is new. At least
15 minutes between runs
sc.schedule.4.b:
A side that cannot be reached shows
as skipped, not as an error. The next
run catches up
sc.phone-sharing.title: Your phone as a server for other devices
sc.phone-sharing.desc: Four steps: switch on the SFTP server in Share over SFTP, add the folders, leave it running - it lasts until you switch it off and resumes whenever the app is shown - and mind the mobile data other devices use.
sc.phone-sharing.sub: At home it opens directly; from outside through Access from anywhere or via Google Drive
sc.phone-sharing.1.b:
Settings, General, Share over SFTP, then
SFTP server. A notification shows it
and has a Stop button
sc.phone-sharing.2.b:
Pick folders with the system picker.
A folder you add joins at once
sc.phone-sharing.3.b:
On until you switch it off. It resumes
whenever the app is shown, also as
the launcher. No start after a reboot
sc.phone-sharing.4.b:
Android 15 may pause it after about 6
hours a day in the background. Mobile
data is billed by your operator
sc.my-devices.title: Add your exchange server in My devices
sc.my-devices.desc: Six steps: open My devices, add the server by pasting a string, scanning a QR code or choosing a file, trust its certificate, sign in with a password or a pairing code, pass the server on to your other devices, then choose the outgoing server.
sc.my-devices.sub: The string and the QR code carry the address and the certificate - never a login or a password
sc.my-devices.1.b:
Settings, General, My devices,
then Add server
sc.my-devices.2.b:
A server string, a QR code or a file -
or type address, login and password
sc.my-devices.3.b:
Trust it only if the fingerprint
matches the one your server shows
sc.my-devices.4.b:
Password, or a pairing code from
another device: one use, ten minutes
sc.my-devices.5.b:
Pass the server on by QR code or text.
It never carries a login or password
sc.my-devices.6.b:
Make outgoing: this phone publishes
through it. Attach everything
automatically is in the same menu
